summary: BRAINSTORM/s6_window_independence.md already proves (Prop, trivial) that for windows m≠m′, gcd(K_m,K_{m′}) divides (m−m′)/4, i.e. the forced-failure sets of distinct windows are coprime-structured and act as independent lotteries; the 'three-window algebraic relation' is therefore the same gcd constraint applied to triples, and the memo's conclusion (windows are independent, so no algebraic relation makes simultaneous avoidance impossible) answers the item.

summary: Checked, for p∈{9 (★)-failing primes ≤10⁶, 4 controls} and C≤100 (1300 pairs (p,C)): 1276 levels have L_C=0. For 980 of them −1 ∉ ⟨prime factors of 4Cp+1⟩ mod 4C (an algebraic/index obstruction, the same as the subgroup argument); for 296 (23%) −1 lies in the generated subgroup, so the failure is combinatorial (no subset of the prime factors multiplies to −1). Only 24 levels are nonempty (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z2952_Z2957_Z2962.py; out z2952_2957_2962_out.txt). So a sizeable share of level failures is not explained by subgroup index, which is the part a subgroup/Kneser-type argument cannot reach.
not_done: Only C≤100 and 13 primes; index [G:H] not tabulated; no test whether the combinatorial share persists as C grows (the item's index study at C≤100 is done only in this coarse form).
next: Repeat for C up to 10⁴ on p≤10⁶ and report the combinatorial share as a function of C (is it decreasing?).
